nodes.summary: For a map $\varphi$ from $T$ to words over $T'$ and a letter $a \in T$, the block of $a$ is the word over the disjoint union $T \sqcup T'$ that consists of $a$, as a letter of $T$, followed by the letters of $\varphi(a)$, as letters of $T'$.
nodes.title: Block of a letter

nodes.summary: Erasing right letters is the map from letters of the disjoint union $T \sqcup T'$ to words over $T$ that sends a letter $a$ of $T$ to the one-letter word $a$ and every letter of $T'$ to the empty word.
nodes.title: Erasing right letters

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ and let $T$ be a finite alphabet. If $g$ derives a sentential form $y$ from a sentential form $x$, then the marker-insertion grammar of $g$ over $T \sqcup T'$ derives the translation of $y$ from the translation of $x$, where a sentential form is translated by replacing each of its symbols by its marker translation.
nodes.title: The marker-insertion grammar simulates the original grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ and let $T$ be a finite alphabet. For every word $u$ over $T \sqcup T'$, the marker-insertion grammar of $g$ derives $u$ from the marked form of $u$, the sentential form that lists the letters of $u$ from $T'$ in order, each preceded by the marker nonterminal $D$, followed by one more $D$.
nodes.title: Marker loops fill in the left letters

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ and let $T$ be a finite alphabet. The marker-insertion grammar of $g$ generates exactly the words $u$ over $T \sqcup T'$ whose letters from $T'$, read in order, form a word of the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Language of the marker-insertion grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ with start symbol $A_0$, and let $T$ be a finite alphabet. The marker-insertion grammar of $g$ is the context-free grammar over $T \sqcup T'$ whose nonterminals are those of $g$ together with a new start symbol $S$ and a marker $D$, and whose rules are: for each rule $A \to \alpha$ of $g$, the rule $A \to \alpha'$, where $\alpha'$ is $\alpha$ with $D$ inserted in front of…
nodes.title: Marker-insertion grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ and let $T$ be an alphabet. Each symbol of $g$ is translated to a string of symbols with terminals in $T \sqcup T'$ and nonterminals those of $g$ together with two new nonterminals $S$ and $D$: a terminal $b \in T'$ becomes the marker $D$ followed by $b$, and a nonterminal $A$ of $g$ becomes $A$.
nodes.title: Marker translation of a symbol

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$ and let $T$ be an alphabet. This valuation assigns a language over $T \sqcup T'$ to each nonterminal of $g$ and to the two new nonterminals $S$ and $D$ of the marker-insertion grammar of $g$: to the marker $D$ the words with no letter from $T'$; to the new start symbol $S$ the words whose letters from $T'$ form a word of the language of $g$; and to a nonterminal $A$ of…
nodes.title: Valuation for the marker-insertion grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar over $T'$, let $T$ be an alphabet, and let $u$ be a word over $T \sqcup T'$. The marked form of $u$ is the sentential form, with terminals in $T \sqcup T'$ and nonterminals those of $g$ together with two new nonterminals $S$ and $D$, that lists the letters of $u$ from $T'$ in order, each preceded by the marker $D$, followed by one more $D$.
nodes.title: Marked form of a word

nodes.summary: Context-free languages are closed under inverse homomorphisms from a finite alphabet.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under inverse homomorphisms

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet and let $L$ be a context-free language over an alphabet $T'$. Then the language of words $u$ over the disjoint union $T \oplus T'$ whose letters from $T'$, read in order, form a word of $L$ is context-free.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under inserting letters

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet, $T'$ an alphabet, $\sigma \colon T^* \to {T'}^*$ a morphism of free monoids and $L$ a context-free language over $T'$. Then the inverse image $\sigma^{-1}(L) = \{x \in T^* \mid \sigma(x) \in L\}$ is a context-free language over $T$.
nodes.title: Context-free languages are closed under inverse free-monoid morphisms

nodes.summary: For a word $u$ over the disjoint union $T \oplus T'$ of two alphabets, its right projection is the word over $T'$ obtained from $u$ by deleting every letter from $T$ and reading each remaining letter as a letter of $T'$, keeping their order.
nodes.title: Right projection of a word

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
